note: These cases specify required service behavior. The build script checks its registry/fixture consistency only; it does not implement the classifier, SQL parser, source ownership, authorization, snapshot or inventory services.

cases.name: Exactly one primary assignment
cases.given: Two assignments give different primary types to the same item occurrence, revision and classification generation.
cases.expected: Reject the conflicting assignment; do not select by embedding score or store simultaneous primary types. Different revisions/generations retain explicit separate assignments.

cases.name: Immutable registry and explicit DAG
cases.given: A type ID is redefined, an is_a target is unknown, or the published subtype graph contains a cycle.
cases.expected: Reject registry publication. Changed meanings require new immutable identities/releases; names, contains and derived_from do not add implicit subtype edges.

cases.name: Exact default and explicit descendants
cases.given: Query dt:file without include_subtypes against file.agents_md and file.sql_declared fixtures, then query with include_subtypes=true.
cases.expected: The exact query does not include either subtype; the descendant query includes both. Page size never changes the selection predicate.

cases.name: AGENTS.md role does not establish parse or authority
cases.given: A checked file is named AGENTS.md but its payload has invalid UTF-8 or untrusted instructions; another is named agents.md.
cases.expected: The first may retain the exact filename-role type while text decoding fails; do not infer Markdown, trust, applicability or instruction authority. Lowercase agents.md does not match the registered case-exact rule.

cases.name: Opaque bytes and unresolved format are distinct
cases.given: One payload is explicitly opaque; another has known bytes but unknown format; a third has no established primary kind.
cases.expected: Use raw_binary_data, bytes with unresolved format assessment, and unresolved respectively. Neither unresolved state matches every type or proves a completed nonmatch.

cases.name: Whole strict JSON profile
cases.given: Inputs include duplicate object keys, NaN, Infinity, trailing non-whitespace, malformed JSON, and a valid full JSON scalar.
cases.expected: Duplicate keys are a profile rejection, not asserted to violate JSON grammar. Non-JSON constants, trailing junk and malformed syntax fail validation. The valid scalar document is allowed. No partial parse becomes a validated JSON document.

cases.name: Exact numeric lexical typing
cases.given: JSON contains 9007199254740993, 1, 1.0, 1e0, true, the string 1, and -0.
cases.expected: Preserve precision; integer-form lexemes become integer, dot/exponent forms decimal, Boolean and string stay distinct. Preserve source -0 while canonicalizing integer value to 0. Do not round through binary float.

cases.name: Equal values at distinct locations
cases.given: JSON /limits/0 and /limits/1 both contain integer 3.
cases.expected: Return two item occurrences with distinct IDs/locators; do not merge them because their values or content hashes match.

cases.name: Parent and locator consistency
cases.given: A child points at the wrong parent, wrong document revision, mismatched escaped JSON Pointer, or a parent member/index not naming it.
cases.expected: Reject the inconsistent view. Verify immediate containment, root linkage and immutable source owner/revision, including ~0 and ~1 escaping.

cases.name: Eager registered materialization and bounded failure
cases.given: A registered JSON source exceeds a node/depth/numeric budget or its materializer fails halfway.
cases.expected: Retain explicit partial/failed itemisation with reasons. Default policy attempts every nested registered value; do not mark the parent complete or claim every integer is indexed.

cases.name: No recursive catalog self-indexing
cases.given: The catalog contains integer page_size, generation metadata, type registry entries and itemisation child counts.
cases.expected: Do not recursively turn this bookkeeping into user data items. Only payloads/fields selected by a registered source materializer are in scope.

cases.name: Containment and derivation do not confer type
cases.given: A JSON document contains integers and a file has linked bytes/text/SQL representations.
cases.expected: The document is not an integer, and the file is not a parsed document or bytes item merely through links. Each explicit representation has its own primary type.

cases.name: SQL declaration and validated syntax
cases.given: A .sql file has invalid syntax, unknown dialect, or only a successfully parsed prefix; another fully parses under a pinned dialect/parser release.
cases.expected: The file role may remain declared SQL; only the complete successful parse yields a SQL document. Never execute input to classify it or infer semantic validity, permission, or execution success.

cases.name: Agent definition descendant isolation
cases.given: Query agent.definition with descendants over role/composite definitions, a deployment and a run.
cases.expected: Return only definition descendants. Coordination/planning/research/coding/review/verification-assistance/memory-curation subtypes are available; deployment/run types are separate branches.

cases.name: Composite agent declarations
cases.given: An agent definition explicitly declares coding and review roles; another source merely claims it has powerful tools.
cases.expected: The first has exactly one composite primary type with declared role facets. A role-filtered definition query can find it; it does not silently inherit every role subtype. Neither role nor tool claim grants capability or policy authority.

cases.name: Workflow definition descendant isolation
cases.given: Query workflow.definition with descendants over coding/research/verification/memory-curation/evaluation/deployment definitions, composites and runs.
cases.expected: Return only definitions, preserving declared-kind facets. A workflow.run references its checked definition but never becomes a definition subtype; deployment workflow type does not authorize deployment.

cases.name: Checked owner and execution references
cases.given: An item has multiple owners, an agent deployment points at a workflow definition, an agent run names a definition different from its deployment's definition, or a workflow run names a deployment as its definition.
cases.expected: Reject every inconsistent or unauthorized binding. Each catalog item is a checked view of exactly one existing owner; it never becomes a parallel execution/verification truth record.

cases.name: Stable occurrence snapshot and authenticated cursor
cases.given: New items arrive, an existing file is renamed/reclassified, or a client changes filters/generation/principal while resuming a cursor.
cases.expected: Original pages retain frozen membership and stable key order without skips or duplicates. Authenticated cursor binds principal, manifest, registry, generation and filter fingerprint; reject changed selectors and require a new query/snapshot.

cases.name: Access and deletion changes
cases.given: Access is revoked or a relevant deletion boundary changes after page one.
cases.expected: Invalidate the cursor and require restart under a new authorized snapshot. Do not deliver stale content or leak revoked memberships/counts/existence. All coverage counts concern only the authorized scope.

cases.name: Independent completeness dimensions
cases.given: Delivery reaches its final page but ingestion/classification/itemisation is partial, or the query times out/cancels before final delivery.
cases.expected: Report selection, ingestion, classification, itemisation and delivery separately. Final delivery alone cannot establish exhaustive scoped typed occurrences; timeout/cancellation never silently claims completion.
